title: Finite scalar coordinates for twisted coherent global sections
statement: Let k be a field, P=Proj k[x_0,x_1] [def-sc-p1-standard], and G a coherent O_P-module [pqf-def-coherent]. For every n in N, there are r in N and an additive equivalence e: Gamma(P,G tensor O_P(n)) -> (Fin r -> k) such that multiplication by any constant homogeneous polynomial C(c) using G tensor twistMul [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], transported along n+0=n, is sent by e to coordinatewise multiplication by c. The assertion is independent of any representing graded polynomial module.

source.place: Stacks Project, Lemma 01YS(3) and proof of (5), https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01YS; online text read

proof.text: Cover polynomial Proj by its two degree-one basic opens. On each, O(n) is rank one; thus tensoring G with O(n) preserves coherence. Transport by the Proj chart isomorphism and the shifted-free twist identification to a coherent module on the standard projective line. Apply finiteDimensional_H in degree zero and the H-zero/global-sections equivalence. Choose a finite basis and its coordinate additive equivalence e to k^r.

On local homogeneous fractions, twistMul by C(c) is multiplication by the image of c in the structure ring. Its tensor product with G therefore acts by c on twisted sections. The coordinate additive equivalence comes from a k-linear basis equivalence and takes this action to coordinatewise scalar multiplication. Transport along n+0=n gives the displayed equality; proof irrelevance makes it independent of p. If the section space is zero choose r=0; n=0 needs no separate argument.
